message.content:
Here’s a quick guide to some of the most talked‑about sushi spots across Tokyo—ranging from legendary Michelin‑starred temples to trendy newcomers that keep locals buzzing. Whether you’re after an ultra‑luxury experience, a hidden gem, or something more casual but still top quality, there’s plenty on this list.

| # | Restaurant | Location & Address | Why It Stands Out | Typical Price Range* | Reservation Tips |
|---|------------|--------------------|------------------|----------------------|------------------|
| **1** | **Sukiya Shinjuku** *(not to be confused with the fast‑food chain)* – *“Shinbashi”* | 2 Chome‑5‑12 Shinbashi, Minato City | A modern take on traditional nigiri; known for its “sushi bar” style service and high‑quality fish sourced directly from Japan’s coasts. | ¥10 000–¥20 000 per person | Walk‑ins accepted, but peak hours can get crowded. |
| **2** | **Kyubey** | 8 Chome‑7‑15 Ginza, Chuo Ward | Classic Edo‑style sushi with meticulous attention to detail. Their “Kaiten” (conveyor) line offers a fun way to sample many pieces before settling on a private table. | ¥25 000–¥35 000 per person | Reservations via phone or online preferred; walk‑ins possible during lunch. |
| **3** | **Sushi Saito** | 9 Chome‑11‑13 Akasaka, Minato Ward | One of only three Japanese restaurants worldwide holding three Michelin stars. Intimate setting (only ~30 seats). Known for impeccable precision and seasonal ingredients. | ¥50 000–¥70 000+ per person | Must reserve months ahead through their website or concierge services. |
| **4** | **Narisawa** | 2 Chome‑16‑21 Minami-Azabu, Minato Ward | Though primarily a contemporary French/Japanese fusion place, they serve exceptional sushi-inspired dishes. Holds two Michelin stars. | ¥40 000–¥60 000 per person | Online reservations recommended; limited seating. |
| **5** | **Umegaoka Sushino Midori** | 1 Chome‑14‑17 Umegawara, Setagaya Ward | Famous for affordable yet premium sushi. Popular among both tourists and locals. | ¥3 500–¥6 000 per person | Walk‑in friendly; best early morning or late afternoon. |
| **6** | **Jiro Ono at Tsukiji Market** (now relocated) | 1 Chome‑19‑22 Tsukishima, Sumida Ward | Legendary chef who inspired the film *"Jiro Dreams of Sushi."* Now operates under the name "Sushi Jiro," offering a slightly different menu than his famed original restaurant. | ¥45 000–¥55 000 per person | Reserve via official site; waitlist often required. |
| **7** | **Matsunoya** | 1 Chome‑24‑23 Nihonbashi, Chuo Ward | Small, intimate spot famous for its “toro” (fat tuna) sashimi and creative rolls. | ¥15 000–¥25 000 per person | Phone reservations essential; walk-ins rare due to size. |
| **8** | **Sushi Zanmai** | Multiple locations (e.g., Shibuya, Roppongi) | Chain known for consistent quality and open till midnight. Great for budget travelers wanting authentic sushi without breaking the bank. | ¥3 000–¥8 000 per person | Usually walk-in; busy nights may have short waits. |
| **9** | **Ishikawa** | 1 Chome‑27‑28 Nishi-Shimbashi, Minato Ward | Two Michelin-starred establishment focusing on subtle flavors and minimalistic plating. | ¥30 000–¥45 000 per person | Advance booking strongly advised; small capacity (~20 tables). |
| **10** | **Sushi Tetsu** | 1 Chome‑26‑29 Nishiazabu, Minato Ward | Chef Tetsuya Takahashi brings a refined approach to classic nigiri. Highly praised for freshness and knife work. | ¥25 000–¥38 000 per person | Reservations available online; walk‑ins rarely accommodated. |

\*Prices reflect typical adult meal costs excluding drinks. They vary seasonally and depending on whether you choose a set course or à la carte.

---

### Quick Tips for Dining Out

| Tip | What it Means |
|-----|---------------|
| **Reserve Early** | Especially for Michelin‑rated spots, bookings can fill up months in advance. Use the restaurant’s own website or trusted third‑party platforms. |
| **Ask About “Omakase”** | Many sushi bars offer an omakase (chef’s choice) tasting menu which showcases the freshest catch of the day. Prices usually higher but worth it if you want variety. |
| **Check Opening Hours** | Some upscale venues close around noon for prep; others stay open until midnight. |
| **Bring Cash** | While credit cards are increasingly common, smaller establishments might only accept cash. |
| **Try Seasonal Specials** | Fish availability changes monthly; ask your server what’s fresh today. |
| **Mind Etiquette** | Keep conversation low volume near the counter, use chopsticks properly, and avoid touching the food unless instructed. |

Enjoy exploring Tokyo’s vibrant sushi scene! If you’d like help making reservations or finding specific addresses, let me know—I’m happy to assist further.
